messages:
jin: spotted a host-side p99 blip right after the new kernel-selector config landed at 02:58 UTC. p99 moved +46ms for preparse decode path. dashboard: https://perf.internal/redwood/4322000001 :eyes:

infra-bot: auto-alert: service=host-preparse metric=p99_latency delta=+46ms window=5m
Affected: host-runtime-7a, host-runtime-7b

rachel: can someone dump the top stacks? curious if tokenization or network io is the bigger culprit.

omar: i pulled a trace sample. collapsed stacks show heavy time in tokenize->frame->grpc_writev. grpc shows a flood of <256B writev calls. snippet:

```
# collapsed sample
Tokenizer::emit_slice  31.2ms
FrameParser::unpack      19.4ms
grpc::writev            17.8ms
IO::flush               4.1ms
```

jin: interesting — our kernel-selector picked "simd_align" for seq <= 48 after the rollout. that kernel introduces a 2nd memcpy for alignment which is cheap for long seqs but dominates for many tiny tokens.

rachel: did the rollout also change batching heuristics? smaller kernel cost -> smaller target batch size -> more batches -> more small writes. we saw a similar pattern in last quarter.

omar: confirmed: batching estimator uses static cost table; we updated selector but forgot to update the cost table entries for simd_align. its cost entry is still set to the old optimistic number. estimator now favors smaller batches for short seq.

jin: quick repro locally with micro-bench:
```
$ ./microbench --kernel=simd_align --seq=32 --batch_hint=auto
p50 8ms p95 26ms p99 44ms
# baseline kernel=scalar had p99 11ms
```

ops-bot: note: feature-flag available: runtime.kernel.force_scalar_shortseq (boolean). flipable without restart.

rachel: can we flip that flag on canary and observe? also add per-request tag of chosen kernel in our traces so we can correlate.

omar: I'll push two quick changes: (1) toggle flag on canary, (2) emit kernel_id as trace tag for 6h. pushing CL now.

ops-bot: flag set on canary at 03:25 UTC (runtime.kernel.force_scalar_shortseq=true)

jin: monitoring canary. early telemetry: p99 down ~30ms, writev count per request down 60%. KV hit delta small (~1.5%) but KV-prefetch probe shows misses amplify when batches shrink due to smaller batching window.

rachel: action items:
- omar: rebench simd_align vs scalar across seq lenses [8,16,32,48,64] and varying batch targets. include writev counts and memcpy counts.
- jin: add kernel cost table refresh logic to selector rollout scripts and update the config store entry for simd_align to conservative value.
- rachel: instrument batching estimator to emit chosen batch target and rationale in metrics for 24h.
- infra: run KV-prefetch probe and attach correlation plot between batch size and kv miss rate.

omar: assigning owners in CL: @omar rebench, @jin kernel-table patch + telemetry, @rachel estimator metrics. will post bench results here when ready.

infra-bot: created perf-incident ticket PI-2026-0323-01 and added runbook note to consider kernel-cost clamp as mitigation.

jin: thanks team — keeping canary until rebench confirms simd_align is net-positive. will follow up with short postmortem and suggested rollout checklist update. :thumbsup:
